newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Telefonica Argentina to resume billing.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica Argentina to resume billing.

text.p: Telefonica de Argentina will resume billing its clients in August for the first time since a court ruled against a new rate structure in February, a spokesman said Friday.

Telefonica's move comes after a court granted it the right to appeal to the Supreme Court an earlier ruling by Judge Liliana Heiland, who ordered the firm not to apply the new rates, the spokesman told Reuters.
Under Argentine law, the fact that Telefonica has been granted the right to appeal the ruling suspends it until the Supreme Court issues its verdict.
In the interim, Telefonica will be applying its new rate structure. It was not clear when the Supreme Court might take up the case.
Argentina's two largest telecommunications firms, Telefonica and Telecom Argentina, tried to overhaul their rate structure after the government granted them authorization by decree in January.

However, the changes -- which cut long-distance rates but increased local call charges -- provoked conflicting court rulings, with legal action taken against the new rate structure by consumer groups and opposition politicians.

Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez, echoing the government's adversarial relationship with Judge Heiland, advised the two telecoms in April to apply the new rates and ignore her ruling until the Supreme Court settled the matter.
Telefonica's rival Telecom, in a different legal strategy, has appealed Heiland's ruling, and has never stopped billing its clients at the new rates.
In another development, Telefonica said on July 1 that Heiland was fining it $40,000 a day, backdated to early March, for not billing its customers.
Telefonica's clients have built up around $300 million in arrears since the beginning of the year s a result of the company not billing, the firm spokesman said.
Telefonica is controlled by Spain's Telefonica de Espana, and Telecom by France Telecom.
